record.title_md: [Informal Conjecture (second phase transition for all radii)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.14218)

dossier_meta.catalog_title: Informal Conjecture (second phase transition for all radii)
dossier_meta.statement_text: It seems likely that for every radius $r$ there should be a second phase transition around some threshold $t=t(n)$. By which we mean that, if $p=\omega(t(n))$, then $G$ is with high probability reconstructible from its $r$-neighbourhoods, while if $p=o(t(n))$ and $p=\omega(n^{-\frac{2r+1}{2r}})$, then with high probability $G$ is not reconstructible from its $r$-neighbourhoods.
dossier_meta.context_text: The paper establishes the existence of this second phase transition for all $r\geq 3$, but the question remains open for $r=1$ and $r=2$, for which only improved (but not matching) bounds are given.
